reason: The capillary knots and surrounding capsules look like the parts of the kidney filters needed for the goal.
expectation: I expect them to form paired filters that let some substances leave the blood, though I don't yet know how the game will show that.

alternatives.reason: The tubule lining also seems necessary for reclaiming substances, but I chose to start with the filters.

effect: The filters let glucose and water through along with urea, so the tubules need a way to reclaim useful substances.
reaction: Seeing useful glucose enter the filter makes the need for recovery clear.
reason: The reabsorbing cells should give the tubules a lining that can reclaim substances; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect to create lined tubules able to reabsorb useful substances, though their connection to the blood may still be needed.

effect: The lined tubules complete the first goal; they now need to be connected to filtration and blood.
reaction: The folded surfaces facing the fluid make their role easier to picture.
reason: Connecting the filters to the tubules should give filtered fluid a route into the recovery section.
expectation: I expect the paired filters and tubules to form a continuous path for filtered fluid; recovery capillaries may still need to be added.

alternatives.reason: The recovery capillaries also seem necessary to return substances to blood, but I chose to connect the fluid path first.

effect: The filters now connect to the lined tubules, creating a route for filtered fluid; recovery capillaries are still needed to connect it to blood.
reaction: The continuous path is clear, though the result adds little beyond what I expected.
reason: The recovery capillaries appear to provide a route back to the blood, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the capillaries to connect alongside the tubules so useful substances can return to the blood.

effect: The recovery vessels return glucose and much of the water to blood, while the remaining fluid continues through the tubule. The next goal is to give that fluid a route out.
reaction: The distinction between filtering and reclaiming useful substances is clear and satisfying.
reason: The urine outflow tract should connect the kidneys to a route out of the body; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the kidneys to connect to the ureters, bladder and urethra, allowing the remaining fluid to leave as urine.

effect: The urinary system now has a route from the kidneys to outside; it still needs to connect to the body's blood supply.
reaction: The route is clear, though it matches what I expected.
reason: Connecting the urinary system to the body should complete the new goal; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the kidneys to connect to the body's circulation so they can filter blood and return reclaimed substances.

effect: The kidneys are now connected to the body's blood supply, completing the chapter. Blood circulates through them repeatedly while urine follows a separate route out.
reaction: The separate routes are clear, although the final connection was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the recovery capillaries made the central idea clear: filtration lets useful glucose through, and tubules reclaim it along with much of the water.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the filters to the tubules felt like a predictable assembly step; its result added little beyond the expected continuous path.

surprise.text: I found it interesting that useful glucose enters the filter with water and urea before being reclaimed.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: each contributed to a filter, recovery route, urine outlet or blood connection. Most choices were offered as compatible combinations, so their compatibility was not something I discovered.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how another body system connects to this model. The filter-and-recovery distinction held my interest, though the mostly predictable assembly steps make me less curious about the individual choices.
